category_title: Elementary students with pragmatic language impairments who struggle with turn-taking and engagement
student_description: James is a student with a learning disability who struggles with pragmatic language during cooperative group work, often impulsively interrupting when he knows an answer and physically withdrawing (e.g., rolling on his back, crossing arms) when corrected. He uniquely requires explicit validation of his academic knowledge before receiving social correction, as well as direct modeling and proactive rehearsal of social rules to prevent the confusion he experiences from ambiguous feedback.

criteria.rationale: James struggles to navigate group dynamics independently and needs to practice language forms and social responses in a safe context before applying them in high-stakes peer groups.
criteria.check: The tutor's plan includes coaching or rehearsing specific questions, answers, or social interactions with James prior to his participation in cooperative group work.

criteria.rationale: James cannot infer social rules through trial-and-error and requires the mechanics of conversation (like listening vs. talking) to be explicitly defined.
criteria.check: The tutor incorporates direct, explicit teaching of specific conversational rules (e.g., defining exactly when to listen and when to talk) within the naturalistic setting.
